content.summary_of_the_paper: A combination of multiple base models with extra convolution layers is used with Fashion-MNIST.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper is not written clearly, in both English usage and overall presentation, making the motivation and potential contributions difficult to follow.

It appears the approach is a fusion ensemble of six efficientnet variants, combined with a multi-layer classification head with branches for standard convolutions with residuals and channelwise-depthwise separable convolutions.  The use of six efficientnet variants would seem to result in a very large model, but gets only 1% improvement over any individual model --- a small but reasonably expected gain for a standard ensemble of several models.

The system is evaluated only on the Fashion-MNIST dataset, and missing many controlled baselines and ablations, such as efficientnet without MCN head and fusions with fewer efficientnets.  In addition, the method combines two or three standard techniques (fusion, ensemble, convolution and separable convolution blocks) with no clear new insights that are specific to this particular combination or task/dataset.
content.summary_of_the_review: The system seems to combine two or three standard techniques (fusion, ensemble, convolution and separable convolution blocks) with no clear new insights that are specific to this particular combination or task/dataset.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a fusion method for transfer learning with a mixed convolution block, including the residual convolution and separable convolution blocks. The proposed method is to modify the existing CNN model with the enhancement network, including Residual Convolution Block (RCB) and Separable Convolution Block (SCB), and the procedure for the three networks such as feature extraction, enhancement, and dense networks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
In the beginning, the paper lists several existing research tasks in the introduction section, but there is no clear description to introduce what problem the proposed method is trying to solve, what are the connections among the existing work, etc. 
The organization of the paper may need to improve. The contribution of this paper may be limited. The authors adopt the RCB and SCB to the proposed DTLMCN with the EfficientNet for transfer learning. However, in the result section, there is only a 1% gain in accuracy (Table 1), and there is no ablation study to discuss what and how the proposed network, module brings the gain. Moreover, the paper is about transfer learning, there are no clear experiments on it.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clear to read, but the novelty is limited. It may not be a well-organized paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: A simple method is always welcome when it works. If the authors can provide more experimental results to show and discuss how and why the simple idea/combination works, it'll make this paper more valuable, including a deep discussion about the proposed method such as the comprehensive ablation study.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes augmenting models trained on ImageNet with an additional network that learns to fuse pretrained features with those learned on the new task. It experiments using the Fashion-MNIST dataset using the pretrained EfficientNet model. Experiments show an improvement of 1% in terms of accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The idea of fusing pretrained weights with domain learned weights sounds interesting.

Weaknesses:
- The approach is only evaluated on a single dataset which is not as complex as real-world datasets. 
- The accuracy improvement of 1% for this dataset is small and it is necessary to show a consistent improvement across a variety of datasets.
- There are no results on the computational aspects and how the additional network can hinder the overall performance in terms of latency. 
- There is a large body of work on transfer learning more optimally which should be compared against as well.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- There is no clear explanation on why the two particular branches res and depth-wise are needed. The use of pointwise convolutions as mentioned in the paper for mixing purposes has also been proposed in other works. An ablation study is missing to show the importance of each part. 
- Not clear if the training parameters and settings are those used by related works as well. If not, then it is not clear if this is the reason for the improvement of accuracy since the margin of 1% is small.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper currently has a lot of room for improvement as it is limited in many ways. First, the motivation behind the proposed structure of the feature enhancement network is not properly justified with the relevant ablation studies. Second, it seems that the approach is very relevant to transfer learning hence, more targeted comparisons are needed with more works and datasets. Third, the accuracy improvement of 1% does not seem significant under the current settings. Finally, only the accuracy improvement aspect is explore omitting, other factors such as additional computational and memory requirements.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a fusion model for better accuracy classification. The model consists of two modules: residual and separable convolutions. Experiments are conducted using Fashion-MNIST.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Weakness]
I strongly recommend that the authors proofread their draft before submission. There are uncountable number of grammatical mistakes and unnatural expressions. This shows the authors did not pay much attention to the paper revision. “Will ask professional English check if accepted” will not help because this should have been done before the first submission.

Experimental validation is far from satisfactory. The authors used only a single dataset: Fashion-MNIST. To show the generality of the proposed model, it is mandatory to conduct experiments with multiple datasets. In addition, although the authors claim fusion models are getting more attention in 2.3, technical survey nor comparison to them is presented. Therefore, the authors failed to convince the reviewer of the validity of the proposed method.

The logical structure should also be modified. In the introduction, the number of parameters and the efficiency were emphasized in the abstract and the introduction, but no discussion has been provided after that. In the experiments, the authors only compare classification accuracy. Therefore, it is not clear what the fundamental contribution of the paper is.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
It might be reproducible because the network architecture is clearly shown though I did not check it by myself.
I have a strong concern about the clarity, quality, and novelty of the paper as I have summarized above.
content.summary_of_the_review: I recommend rejection of this paper with a strong confidence. Please have a look at the weakness section.
